import os
import subprocess
import sys

from sase.vcs_provider import get_vcs_provider

checkout_target = {{ setup.checkout_target | tojson }}
project_name = {{ setup.project_name | tojson }}
gh_ref = {{ gh_ref | tojson }}

provider = get_vcs_provider(os.getcwd())

# Checkout the PR branch so that subsequent diffs are relative to the
# PR tip rather than the default branch. Try checkout_target first
# (works for default-branch refs like origin/main), then fall back to
# Patch name -> branch name conversion.
is_patch = checkout_target == f"origin/{gh_ref}"
ok, err = provider.checkout(checkout_target, os.getcwd())
if not ok:
    if is_patch:
        # Patch ref — resolve name to branch name
        resolved = provider.resolve_revision(
            gh_ref, project_name, os.getcwd()
        )
        ok, err = provider.checkout(resolved, os.getcwd())
    else:
        # Project/repo ref — try common default branch names
        for fallback in ["master", "main"]:
            ok, err = provider.checkout(fallback, os.getcwd())
            if ok:
                break
    if not ok:
        print(
            f"Warning: checkout failed: {err}",
            file=sys.stderr,
        )

# Sync with remote after checkout
subprocess.run(
    ["git", "pull", "--rebase", "--quiet"],
    capture_output=True,
    text=True,
    check=False,
)

# Record HEAD for the diff step
result = subprocess.run(
    ["git", "rev-parse", "HEAD"],
    capture_output=True,
    text=True,
    check=False,
)
head = result.stdout.strip() if result.returncode == 0 else ""
print(f"head_before={head}")
print("success=true")

head_before="{{ checkout.head_before }}"
if [ -z "$head_before" ]; then
  exit 0
fi
head_now=$(git rev-parse HEAD)
diff_dir="${SASE_TMPDIR:-${SASE_HOME:-$HOME/.sase}/tmp}/gh-diffs"
mkdir -p "$diff_dir"
diff_file=$(mktemp "$diff_dir/sase-gh-XXXXXX.diff")
if [ "$head_now" != "$head_before" ]; then
  # Commits were made — show only the last commit's diff
  git diff HEAD~1 HEAD > "$diff_file" 2>/dev/null
  commit_msg=$(git log -1 --format='%s' HEAD)
  echo "meta_commit_message=$commit_msg"
else
  # No commits — show uncommitted changes
  git diff HEAD > "$diff_file" 2>/dev/null
  git ls-files --others --exclude-standard -z 2>/dev/null \
    | while IFS= read -r -d '' f; do
        git diff --no-index /dev/null "$f" 2>/dev/null
      done >> "$diff_file"
fi
if [ -s "$diff_file" ]; then
  echo "diff_path=$diff_file"
else
  rm -f "$diff_file"
fi

# Stash any uncommitted changes (including untracked files)
if ! git diff --quiet HEAD 2>/dev/null || [ -n "$(git ls-files --others --exclude-standard)" ]; then
  git stash push --include-untracked -m "gh-workflow-$(date +%s)" --quiet
  echo "stashed=true"
else
  echo "stashed=false"
fi
git fetch origin --quiet 2>&1 || true
git pull --rebase --quiet 2>/dev/null || true
echo "success=true"

from sase_github.scripts.gh_setup import main
main(
    gh_ref={{ gh_ref | tojson }},
    n={{ n | tojson }},
    release={{ release | tojson }},
    workflow_label={{ workflow_label | tojson }},
)

I’ll first map the pager’s current rendering path and its existing highlighting guarantees, then compare implementation options against the libraries actually in use, write the independent `__a.md` report without touching the peer report, and register that exact file as an artifact.

The central constraint is now clear: the pager already treats styling as input data. ANSI-rendered bead output is parsed into a Rich `Text`, and link-label overlays splice that `Text` while preserving its spans. File inputs, by contrast, arrive as unstyled strings. The design should enrich only those unstyled/file-aware sections and keep the current styled-body path authoritative. I’m checking SASE’s existing syntax helpers and Textual/Rich behavior next, especially large-file cost and search/link-offset stability.

A second design constraint surfaced in testing: Rich/Pygments can normalize the text unless configured carefully—its defaults may add a final newline and expand tabs. That would invalidate every pager link span. The safe form is to instantiate the detected lexer with `stripnl=False`, `ensurenl=False`, and `tabsize=0`, require byte-for-byte-equivalent Unicode text before accepting the highlight result, and fall back to the original styled `Text` on any mismatch or lexer error. This turns “preserve current highlighting” into an enforceable invariant rather than a visual hope.

The report is written and its final recommendation is concrete: preserve one immutable text coordinate space, add lazy Pygments token styles beneath existing ANSI/Rich spans, and keep pager labels/search as the top overlays. It also rejects unrestricted content guessing after finding real false positives (for example, Makefile content guessed as T-SQL) and specifies exact no-normalization/fallback tests. I’m registering the exact report path now, then I’ll verify the returned artifact identity and final repository state.
